correctness.rationale: Every off-diagonal vertex pair shares exactly the two oppositely oriented arcs; conditional on them the four remaining binomial arc counts are independent. Centering the conditional cell probability gives two degree-derivative terms and one bilinear interaction, whose orthogonality yields the exact covariance decomposition. Elementary binomial-score identities give four pairwise orthogonal eigendirections, two zeros, a sharp 2n mode, a n²/(n−1) interaction mode, and n on their orthogonal complement. Boundary n=2, all 0<p<1, rank and multiplicities checked. Standalone exact rational enumeration exhausts n=2,3,4 (12,492 probability-weighted digraph configurations across three probabilities) and every covariance matrix entry, but the general theorem rests on the analytical proof.

evidence: Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2006.15797 gives asymptotic fixed-edge-count labeled degree sequence probabilities in regularity ranges; arXiv:0912.4812 provides exact covariance for undirected single-degree count vectors.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general asymptotic joint degree-sequence approximation does not determine all finite n,p moments or eigenvalues, especially non-typical histogram cells; the undirected single-degree model couples a different edge set and has no reverse-arc interaction. The directed-component scaling theorem addresses connectivity rather than covariance. There is no observed stronger exact theorem covering the full claim.

evidence: Undirected degree-count work yields covariance mechanisms for one degree per vertex; Liebenau–Wormald approximates labeled in-/out-degree sequence distributions with fixed total edges, whereas the present identity is exact for random total edges; Goldschmidt–Stephenson concerns strongly connected components.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Specializing a prior theorem to this object/parameter set would be decisive, but the inspected closest results have different models/statistics or nonexact asymptotics. The new diagonalization requires two oriented shared arcs and the bilinear interaction direction. It cannot be obtained merely by substituting directed labels into the undirected rank-one covariance formula.

evidence: Liebenau–Wormald (arXiv:2006.15797) studies a labeled in-/out-degree sequence under fixed edge count using asymptotic enumeration; Lin–Reinert (arXiv:0912.4812) studies univariate undirected degree-cell counts.

Neither source supplies the stated unconditional finite-n n²-cell covariance and three nonzero eigenvalue levels. An unrecognized implicit equivalent remains a priority risk.

originality.rationale: Under actual retrieved history, targeted result searches and relevant full-text inspections, none of the closest items determines the exact unconditional finite-n Pearson spectrum of the complete directed bidegree histogram. Unlike Lin–Reinert’s exact undirected one-degree count covariance, reverse directed arcs yield a signed rank-two correction plus a bilinear interaction. Liebenau–Wormald’s wider labeled in/out-degree-sequence result is asymptotic and conditioned on edge count, and does not imply the exact unrestricted claim. Earlier general identities may implicitly encode the same result; novelty remains self-review, not independently confirmed.
residual_risks: Exact finite covariance matrix may be derivable in an unlocated general degree-sequence or contingency-table moment theorem.
An equivalent closed spectral form might appear under chi-square/categorical null-test terminology.

value.rationale: Full bidegree histograms are canonical sufficient descriptive data for directed network null models. Their n²-dimensional dependence geometry is not captured by marginal binomial laws: normalization and arc conservation yield exactly two null modes, while symmetric degree and in×out interaction obtain distinct variance inflation; all residual directions have exactly multinomial covariance. A universal, sharp factor-two bound quantifies errors from treating vertices as independent across any linear histogram statistic. This is a structural finite-sample classification, not merely a small numerical refinement. It informs variance modeling without asserting an unproved chi-square or Gaussian limit.
